newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters sets new UPS strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters sets new UPS strike deadline.

text.p: The Teamsters Union said on Saturday that it was setting a new strike deadline for midnight on Sunday in its dispute with United Parcel Service.

"More than 185,000 Teamster members at United Parcel Service will go on strike on Sunday night at midnight (EDT) (0400 GMT on Monday) if the company refuses to agree to a new contract that provides good full-time jobs with pensions and health coverage," the union said in a statement.
The union had originally set a strike deadline for last Thursday but postponed it amid negotiations that were mediated by a federal agency.
"The brown trucks won't be rolling unless this company agrees to provide the good jobs that American families need," Teamsters President Ron Carey said.

Carey said the union was holding out for a contract that would create more full-time jobs that were now part-time, and was pressing the company to stop sub-contracting the work of drivers and to improve pensions, safety and health benefits.

The comments were in a statement issued in Washington. Talks were suspended on Friday night and negotiators have not said when they would resume. Earlier on Saturday United Parcel Service, the largest U.S. package carrier, said it was losing about 8 percent of its daily business because of the possibility of a strike.
